name: Intercom
task: A help desk, tickets or a shared inbox
summary: Customer service platform that combines a helpdesk and shared inbox with the Fin AI agent, priced per seat plus a fee per resolved conversation.
best_for: support teams that want a messenger, shared inbox and an AI agent in one platform, and are fine paying per seat plus per resolved conversation
skip_if: you want one flat monthly price, you have a very small inbox and no need for an AI agent, or you want a tool we have tested through a paid plan ourselves
honest_knock: The bill has two meters: a price per seat and $0.99 for each conversation Fin resolves, so it grows with both team size and volume. Advanced and Expert cost $85 and $132 a seat. The cheaper Essential price is shown as a new-customer offer. We have not paid for a plan, so real-world Fin accuracy is unknown to us.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on intercom.com/pricing, US dollars per seat per month, billed annually) Essential $29 (new customers $19, 35% off), Advanced $85, Expert $132; billed monthly $39, $99 and $139 per seat, per Intercom's help article 'Fin and Intercom plans explained' read the same day; every plan includes the Fin AI Agent, charged at $0.99 per outcome. Fin alone for an existing helpdesk: $0.99 per outcome, no seats, minimum monthly commitment. Early Stage programme: 96% off for startups under $10M raised with 15 employees or fewer. Free trial of 14 days, no credit card required, with Fin and the Pro, Proactive Support Plus and Copilot add-ons included during the trial. We have not paid for a plan.

schema_offer.description: Essential, per seat per month; Advanced $85 and Expert $132 per seat per month; Fin AI Agent $0.99 per outcome on top; new customers see $19 on Essential. Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-17.

Expert Pay annually Collaboration and security features for large support teams. Intercom helpdesk $132 per seat/mo
Intercom helpdesk $29 $19 per seat/mo New customers save 35%

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session linked five help articles of a made up snowboard store to the Fin AI Agent of Intercom under the free 14 day Advanced trial and tested Fin with ten questions in the Batch Test. Fin answered 9 correctly and 1 wrongly, each in about 10 seconds: it said the store does not carry helmets, although none of the articles says so, and it gave Content (4) as its source. Fin never names the article in its answer; only the evaluation panel shows the number of sources. A new article has to be published to the help center and then to Fin before Fin can use it. The prices are unchanged against the dossier (annual Essential $19 for new customers, Advanced $85, Expert $132; monthly $29, $99 and $139; Fin $0.99 per outcome), and the monthly new-customer price of $29 with 25% off is not in the dossier. The payment screen was reached and nothing was entered, and tax was not shown. Account and start: the account was created by us, the interface was already in English and the time zone was Amsterdam (CET); our AI assistant ran the test in his browser from 14:54. The first screen said Your 14-day trial is ready with Intercom helpdesk + Fin AI Agent and a Get started button, and a banner said the Advanced trial ends in 14 days. No card, no phone number, no channel and no mailbox was asked. The dossier name is Intercom and the review is on ZTS (zts/intercom-review.html). The audience from the dossier: small teams that want one inbox with an AI agent; the pain: customers write in through chat and email and I answer the same questions all day. Core action: from 14:56 to 15:00 five help articles for a made up store, Sample Snowboards, were written in Knowledge, Articles (shipping, returns, size chart, board care and waxing, opening hours). No messenger was installed and nothing was connected to a real channel. Hurdle 1: a new article has Fin availability Disabled and grey switches. First Publish to help center has to be switched on, then Publish to Fin Main, and then a choice between In a Help Center (Not live) and As an unlisted public article. The tester chose unlisted, so the Help Center was not made live. After that the page said Your article has been published and Fin availability showed Enabled (3). Hurdle 2: the description field (maximum 255 characters) is a separate field above the body text, and text typed in it by mistake is cut off. This was fixed in 2 articles, and 2 empty drafts called Untitled public article stayed behind. Testing Fin: Fin AI Agent, Test, Batch Test, as a Preview user, with Fin Main on Live. Pasting 10 lines in Add manually made 1 long question, so the ten questions were then entered in ten separate fields. The first answer came at 15:01, about seven minutes after the start at 14:54 and about one minute after the articles were done at 15:00, and every answer took about 10 seconds. Score on ten questions: 9 correct, 0 partly correct and 1 wrong. Correct were standard shipping (5 to 7 business days, $8), free shipping over $150, no return of a waxed board, 30 days to return, board length for 175 cm, the wide board for US size 12 boots, waxing every 5 to 8 days of riding, closed on Sundays, and shipping to the United States and Canada only. The wrong answer was the question about helmets: Fin said we don't carry helmets at the moment, with Content (4) as its source, but nothing in the five articles says that the store does not sell helmets, so Fin should have said that it does not know. Fin also repeated Mountain Time everywhere because that is in our own article, so it follows the article text. Sources: Fin never names the article with its title in the answer. Only the evaluation panel shows This answer uses Content (1) to Content (4) and Guidance (2). Plans: Build your plan, read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026 under the Advanced trial, in US dollars excluding tax. Billed annually, per seat per month: Essential ($29) $19, Advanced ($99) $85, Expert ($139) $132; the banner says New customer offer: Save 35% on Essential seats. Billed monthly: Essential ($39) $29 with the banner Save 25% on Essential seats, Advanced $99, Expert $139. Due today for one Full seat: Advanced annual $1,020/yr, Essential annual $228/yr, Essential monthly $29/mo. Fin AI Agent is listed under Included in all plans at $0.99 per outcome with usage limits. Continue to payment opened a Payment method screen with card fields, an optional Tax ID number and the button Pay now; the tester stopped there and filled in nothing, so tax was never shown. The public page intercom.com/pricing was read again just before this delivery the same day, with the annual and the monthly toggle, and shows the same amounts: annual Essential $29 struck through and $19 with New customers save 35%, Advanced $85, Expert $132; monthly Essential $39 struck through and $29 with New customers save 25%, Advanced $99, Expert $139; Fin AI Agent from $0.99 per Fin outcome, also without seats for an existing helpdesk. The prices are therefore UNCHANGED against the dossier. Deviations against the dossier: the dossier names the new-customer price only for annual billing ($19) and not the monthly new-customer price of $29 with 25% off, and the public page now says Startups get 93% off where the dossier has the Early Stage programme at 96% off (not tested here). The trial of the test account is an Advanced trial of 14 days that ends on Dec 03, 2026 and needs no card. Cancelling: Settings, Subscription, Billing shows Free Trial $0.00 with the trial end date Dec 03, 2026, the plan Advanced Trial 14 days left, three add-ons in trial (Proactive Support Plus, Fin AI Copilot, Pro) and the buttons Change trial and Buy Intercom. There is no card, so there was nothing to cancel and the trial ends by itself. Deleting the workspace is under Settings, Workspace, General, Delete workspace: it asks for your full name, says the workspace will be deleted within 14 days of confirmation and has a button Confirm delete. It was not clicked. Not tested: real customer channels and the messenger, a mailbox, inviting team members, Fin as a separate agent on top of another helpdesk (a Zendesk sync was visible in Knowledge and not touched), the Early Stage programme, tax, billing of outcomes (it was not visible whether the test chats counted as an outcome) and contact with the vendor. Clean up: the account, the workspace and the test data stay: 5 published (unlisted) articles, 2 empty draft articles and 1 batch test created via manual entry with 11 questions, one of them the merged long question. The browser tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: A new article is not available to Fin until you publish it to the help center and then to Fin, with the switches grey at first. Fin answers questions that the articles do not cover with a confident wrong statement, for instance that we do not carry helmets, so add an article for what you do not sell. Fin does not name the article it used, so you must check the answer yourself. The description field of an article is capped at 255 characters and cuts text off. Fin is billed per outcome on top of the seats, and the test did not show whether test chats count.

friction.export_route: No export or reimport was performed; no file was downloaded or examined. The two categorised kit records were not entered; the objects tested were not kit records.

not_tested: Real customer channels, the messenger, a mailbox and inviting team members.
Fin as a separate agent on top of another helpdesk, and the Zendesk sync that was visible in Knowledge.
Whether the test chats counted as a billed outcome, and tax on the order.
The Early Stage programme.
Deleting the workspace, which was looked up but not confirmed, and cancelling a paid plan, because nothing was bought.
Export of a file into a kit, and reimport.

Session and source-reading date: 18 November 2026. Times are CET. The session started at about 14:54 CET. These are approximate tester observations, not benchmark timings. Midnight timestamps are required date anchors, not measured event times.
